title: Tech's Big Week: Pollution and Privacy

slides.headline: Tech's Big Week: Pollution and Privacy
slides.subtitle: From Amazon's massive energy footprint to new privacy rulings, here is the news.

slides.headline: Police tech and privacy rulings
slides.explanation: Flock Safety is reportedly working on dashcams that coach police officers while they drive. Meanwhile, a judge ruled that mass cell tower data dumps are unconstitutional, marking a win for digital privacy.

slides.headline: Must-play indie games to try
slides.explanation: New indie titles like Big Walk and a retro electronics repair sim are hitting the scene this week. These unique games offer a refreshing break from the usual blockbuster releases.

slides.headline: Amazon's new Texas power plant
slides.explanation: Amazon is investing in a gas-burning plant in West Texas to power a new data center. Reports suggest the facility could become one of the largest single sources of greenhouse gas emissions in the U.S.

slides.headline: The climate cost of data centers
slides.explanation: The massive energy demands of modern tech are clashing with climate goals. This Texas project highlights the growing tension between building more digital infrastructure and reducing our carbon footprint.

slides.headline: A newsletter guide to the weird
slides.explanation: The Verge's latest edition of Installer dives into everything from Johnny Knoxville to the history of the bicycle. It is a curated look at the best and most interesting things happening online right now.

caption:
From climate concerns in Texas to shifting digital privacy rules, the tech landscape is moving fast. We've broken down the biggest stories you need to know today. Which of these updates surprised you the most?

title: Global Tensions Rise This Weekend

slides.headline: Global Tensions Rise This Weekend
slides.subtitle: Five quick updates on defense, diplomacy, and conflict zones you should know.

slides.headline: Pentagon Pushes for More Weapons
slides.explanation: The Pentagon is urging defense companies to speed up production to restock depleted weapon supplies. This move highlights the ongoing strain on military resources as global demand for armaments stays high.

slides.headline: Golf Leaders at the Wyndham
slides.explanation: Beau Hossler and Brennan are currently tied for the lead at the Wyndham Championship. With postseason spots on the line, every stroke matters as players battle through weather delays.

slides.headline: Vance Claims Iran Nuclear Success
slides.explanation: Vice President JD Vance recently stated that the U.S. has successfully dismantled Iran's nuclear program and weakened its military capabilities. This assertion marks a significant stance on current Middle East security policy.

slides.headline: Medics Targeted in Ukraine
slides.explanation: Ukrainian emergency workers report that Russian drones are increasingly targeting ambulances and hospitals. These attacks pose a severe threat to the medical staff trying to save lives on the front lines.

slides.headline: Russian Ships Near UK Waters
slides.explanation: The Royal Navy says it spent 25 percent more time monitoring Russian vessels around the UK last month. This increase in activity shows rising tensions and the need for constant maritime surveillance.

caption:
